summary: Lewis County, WA: 1935 L-5 cab and 1947 20-foot L-4 tower, last structure removed 1966; both footings remain, reached by a 3.5-mile open trail.

facts.design: 1935 L-5 cab, then a 20-foot timber tower with L-4 cab in 1947
facts.status_note: Last structure removed in 1966; Willhite says both footings still remain

access.note: Dry Creek Trail from FR20 (Smith Creek Road); Willhite says it is open to motorcycles, hikers, horses, and bicycles

visit.trail_note: Willhite: 3.5-mile trail; take Highway 12 west 4 miles from Packwood to FR20 (Smith Creek Road), then follow it 0.3 miles to the Dry Creek Trail sign. The trail crosses Dry Creek on a log early on.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Gifford Pinchot National Forest

events.note: Panoramic photos taken at 16 feet above ground
20-foot timber tower with L-4 cab on top
Heavy snow; Dry Creek was the first Packwood District lookout to open
Locked up for the season by assistant Ranger Jack Fowler; last Packwood District lookout to close
Manned June 13 after two weeks of dry weather; the fire watcher was brought back down when wet weather returned
Registered June 23, 2012 as US 1314, WA 214; nominated by Ray Kresek

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked: status gone, Lewis County, coordinates, elevation (3,815 ft = 1162.8 m) and FFLOS registration date all agree; no corrections. All four sources agree on the 1935 cab, the 1947 tower and the 1966 removal. The 1960 entry is a one-day activation that the sources describe; no staffing after 1960 is recorded, so the staffing status is 'no longer staffed' as of 1960. Willhite's 'both footings still remain' has no date beyond photo captions that include a 2016 view, so treat it as a source's account rather than a fresh observation. The NGS benchmark note (described 1946) is left out: its source gives the survey agency differently from Willhite. Used 1 WebSearch and 4 distinct pages.
